meaning: Servant of the All-Hearing (one of Allah's 99 names)
origin_notes: Compound of ʿabd (servant) + al-Samīʿ (the All-Hearing, Qur'an 2:127)

meaning: Peace; name of the Prophet-King Solomon
origin_notes: From Semitic root sh-l-m (peace/wholeness). The Qur'anic Prophet Sulaymān (Solomon) was granted dominion over wind, animals, and jinn.
Arabicised form of the Hebrew Avraham. Prophet Ibrāhīm is called Khalīlullāh (the Friend of God) in Islamic tradition.

meaning: Servant of the Almighty / the Most Honourable
origin_notes: al-ʿAzīz is one of the 99 names of Allah, meaning the Invincible, the Almighty (Qur'an 59:23).
Feminine form of Fawzī, from the root f-w-z (to succeed, to attain).

meaning: Beloved; name of the mother of Prophet ʿĪsā (Jesus)
origin_notes: The only woman mentioned by name in the Qur'an. Sūrat Maryam (Chapter 19) is named after her.

meaning: Satisfied; content; pleased with Allah's decree
origin_notes: From the root r-ḍ-y (to be pleased/content). Used in Qur'an 88:9 describing souls in Paradise.

meaning: Very grateful; one who gives thanks abundantly
origin_notes: al-Shakūr is one of the 99 names of Allah (Qur'an 35:30).

meaning: Obedient; compliant; one who follows Allah's commands
origin_notes: From the root ṭ-w-ʿ (to obey). A classical Arabic name indicating religious devotion.

meaning: The holy month of fasting; burning heat
origin_notes: From r-m-ḍ (intense heat). Named after the pre-Islamic hot month. Now the 9th month of the Islamic calendar. Children born in this month are sometimes given this name.
Name of the daughter of the Prophet Muḥammad (peace be upon him). Also the name of a tree with fragrant flowers.
al-Raḥmān is one of the supreme names of Allah (Qur'an 1:1). One of the most beloved names in Islam.
Feminine form of Laṭīf (al-Laṭīf is one of the 99 names of Allah meaning the Most Subtle, Qur'an 6:103). Used as a female personal name.
From s-ʿ-d (to be happy, to be blessed). One of the most common classical Arabic names.
Name of the daughter of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and wife of the Prophet Muḥammad (peace be upon him).
The most common and highly recommended name in Islam. Name of the Prophet's father.
The name of the final Prophet of Islam. From ḥ-m-d (to praise). One of the most common names in the world.

meaning: She who lives; lively; full of life
origin_notes: Wife of the Prophet Muḥammad (peace be upon him) and one of the greatest Islamic scholars. From ʿ-y-sh (to live).
Arabicised form of Hebrew Yosef. The Qur'anic Prophet Yūsuf's story is told in Sūrat Yūsuf (Chapter 12) — described as the most beautiful of stories.

meaning: Mother of Kulthūm; epithet indicating a woman of status
origin_notes: Name of two daughters of the Prophet Muḥammad (peace be upon him). The epithet Umm Kulthūm became a term of honour for a respected woman.
From r-ḥ-m (mercy). A beautiful Qur'anic concept used as a female name.
Name of a wife of the Prophet Muḥammad (peace be upon him) and several female companions. From ṣ-f-w (purity, clarity).
Name of the first wife of the Prophet Muḥammad, the first Muslim, and one of the four greatest women in Islam.
An honorific of the Prophet Muḥammad. From ṣ-f-w (to choose, to purify). Muṣṭafā is one of the Prophet's 99 names.
